sources.content_summary: A2A is a public interoperability contract: discovery, supported interface declarations, standard operations, task lifecycle, errors, and streaming must agree on one protocol model.
key_points: Each supported interface owns its protocolVersion and binding declaration.
JSON-RPC v1 methods use PascalCase and streaming uses SSE.
Messages and artifacts use the official v1 Part model.
misconceptions: Naming a package A2A makes a bespoke RPC API conformant.
tasks/send is the A2A v1 SendMessage operation.
A Promise that eventually returns an artifact proves streaming.

sources.content_summary: A2A declares and transports identity; Prometheus application policy decides whether that identity may read tasks or mutate the graph.
key_points: Credentials travel in HTTP security mechanisms, not plaintext AgentCard fields.
Authentication and authorization execute before graph mutation.
Task lookup must not leak the existence of inaccessible resources.
Agent-provided metadata cannot self-authorize a destructive graph operation.
misconceptions: A valid bearer token authorizes every graph action.
A2A protocol validation replaces tenant, entity, field, and action policy.
Returning forbidden for an inaccessible task is always harmless.

sources.content_summary: A2UI artifacts, deterministic agents, and the TCK prove different layers and must retain exact version and scope labels.
key_points: A2UI v0.9.1 is the renderer baseline but the published dedicated A2A extension contract is v0.8 legacy.
A deterministic agent proves protocol and policy paths without an external model key.
The official SDK should own wire types and transport machinery.
The pinned TCK report must state binding, level, skips, and exclusions.
misconceptions: A structured data part automatically proves the current official A2UI-for-A2A extension.
An LLM API is required to test an agent protocol.
A JSON-RPC TCK pass also certifies REST and gRPC.
